## Project Summary

**What it is for:** An NCLEX-PN (Canadian nursing licensing) remediation planner — a local CLI tool that creates personalized 3–30-day study plans from a student's missed exam questions. It tracks why each question was missed (knowledge gap, misread, scope confusion, test anxiety), detects repeated topics, supports client-need filtering, and includes a local study-group leaderboard for accountability. All personal study journals, missed-question logs, and group records stay local; nothing uploads.

**Rules anyone working on it must follow:**
- Never include paid question-bank text (UWorld, Archer, Kaplan, etc.); only your own notes in your own words.
- All generated study-plan templates must have nursing-scope sign-off from someone with nursing background before the tool is shared with a study group.
- Clinical facts and scope limits must match current PN/RPN provincial regulator guidance—the tool enforces PN/RPN scope (follow plan, teach, monitor, report) and rejects instructions to independently assess or initiate treatment.
- Personal files (journal.json, leaderboard.json, scope_review.json, missed.json) are excluded from Git and stay private.
- Any code change that affects generated template wording triggers a new nursing review.

**What's still owed before sharing:** Formal scope-review sign-off. Dami (nursing professional) verbally approved all 8 templates on 2026-09-24, but the attestation record (`scope_review.json`) is not yet completed—all 8 template reviews still show `"reviewed": false`. The source code was also updated after Dami's verbal approval, so the current SHA-256 hash must be generated and recorded in the review file to mark the review complete. Once that JSON is filled in with Dami's name, date, and the current source hash, the tool is ready to publish and share with the study group.
